Class Numbered

java.lang.Object
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.Numbered
Direct Known Subclasses:
Edge, Explanation, Node, Plan, State
public class Numbered extends Object
A story graph element with a unique sequential long ID number. ID numbers are unique for the type of element, but not across the whole story graph. For example, a story graph cannot have two temporal edges with the same ID number, but it can a temporal edge and an epistemic edge with the same ID number.

A large story graph may have many numbered elements, so their ID numbers are Java long integers. Numbered elements are stored in a custom large array list that can have up to BigArrayList.MAX_CAPACITY elements.

Author:
Stephen G. Ware

  • Method Details

    • hashCode

      public int hashCode()

      The hash code of a numbered element is based on its ID number (specifically, it is calculated using Long.hashCode()). Because ID numbers are unique and sequential among numbered elements of the same type, they can be a perfect hash function. However, when a story graph is modified (for example, pruned) elements may be renumbered. If elements are stored based on their hash codes (for example, in a HashMap hash table), their hash codes may be unreliable after the graph is modified.

      public long getID()
      Returns the unique sequential ID number for this element. ID numbers are unique among numbered elements of the same type, but not unique among the story graph as a whole. For example, a story graph cannot have two temporal edges with the same ID number, but it can have a temporal edge and an epistemic edge with the same ID number.
